I build end-to-end products across web, mobile and 3D. Right now that means 3D signing avatars for [SETU](https://setu.prateekinnovations.com) at Prateek Innovations and a campus booking app at RAIN, plus open-source tools for the Linux desktop in my own time. Based in Kathmandu, studying Computer Science with AI at Sunway College.

### `#` open-source

<a href="https://github.com/BhuwanJoshi-01/wayland-wallpaperengine">
  <picture>
    <source media="(max-width: 640px)" srcset="./assets/oss-wwe-mobile.svg">
    <img src="./assets/oss-wwe.svg" width="100%" alt="wayland-wallpaperengine: Steam Wallpaper Engine wallpapers as a live desktop background on Linux Wayland, including GNOME. An animated desktop shows the wallpaper freezing when an app takes focus, while renderer CPU falls from 13 to 0 percent, GNOME Shell CPU from 22 to 3 percent and GPU from 71 to 7 percent.">
  </picture>
</a>

```bash
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BhuwanJoshi-01/wayland-wallpaperengine/main/install.sh | bash
```

[![Stars](https://img.shields.io/github/stars/BhuwanJoshi-01/wayland-wallpaperengine?style=flat-square&labelColor=0e1116&color=89aacc)](https://github.com/BhuwanJoshi-01/wayland-wallpaperengine/stargazers)
[![CI](https://img.shields.io/github/actions/workflow/status/BhuwanJoshi-01/wayland-wallpaperengine/ci.yml?style=flat-square&labelColor=0e1116&label=CI)](https://github.com/BhuwanJoshi-01/wayland-wallpaperengine/actions/workflows/ci.yml)
[![Last commit](https://img.shields.io/github/last-commit/BhuwanJoshi-01/wayland-wallpaperengine?style=flat-square&labelColor=0e1116&color=f4a97f)](https://github.com/BhuwanJoshi-01/wayland-wallpaperengine/commits/main)
[![Website](https://img.shields.io/badge/website-live-23a55a?style=flat-square&labelColor=0e1116)](https://bhuwanjoshi-01.github.io/wayland-wallpaperengine/)

The load numbers in the card are real measurements.[^1]

<details>
<summary><b>How it works on GNOME</b></summary>

<br>

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    service["wwe.service"] --> run["wwe run<br/>supervisor"]
    run -->|"scene, web"| engine["linux-wallpaperengine"]
    run -->|"video"| mpv["mpv"]
    engine --> window["hidden Wayland window"]
    mpv --> window
    shell["GNOME Shell<br/>+ extension"] -->|"copies it into desktop,<br/>overview and lock screen"| window
    shell -->|"pointer and mute commands"| engine
    shell -->|"freeze while you're<br/>not on the desktop"| run
```

Full write-up: [docs/ARCHITECTURE.md](https://github.com/BhuwanJoshi-01/wayland-wallpaperengine/blob/main/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md)

</details>

<details>
<summary><b>How this README works</b></summary>

<br>

No JavaScript and no third-party card services. Each card is an SVG that animates with CSS, because that's what GitHub lets through an `<img>` tag.

- **Text is outlined.** Fonts are shaped with HarfBuzz and written as glyph paths, so they look the same everywhere, Devanagari included.
- **It respects your settings.** With reduced motion turned on, every card holds still.
- **Phones get their own layouts,** chosen with `<picture>` and a media query.
- **The activity card rebuilds itself daily** from the GitHub API, through [a small Action](./.github/workflows/refresh.yml).
- **The stack colours are prayer flags:** blue, white, red, green and yellow.
- **Also native Markdown:** `<details>`, `<kbd>`, alerts, footnotes, a Mermaid diagram and an STL model.

Rebuild everything with `pip install -r scripts/requirements.txt && python scripts/build.py`.

</details>

[^1]: Measured on an Intel iGPU, comparing the desktop in focus with an app in focus: renderer CPU 13 % to 0 %, GNOME Shell CPU 22 % to 3 %, GPU 71 % to 7 %.
